body.p: There are a few important considerations to take into account, when using Cache for Stack and Code:

ul.li: No special hardware protection is provided to suppress evictions due to snooping.
Use of INVD results in loss of DataStack data. It may be used, when the cache contents need to be invalidated or during NEM tear down to flush the cache.
Use of WBINVD or CLFLUSH is not recommended.
Software is responsible for ensuring that code and data use do not result in the DataStack being evicted.
Software must not perform writes to the code region.
Software must not be self modifying.
Allow GET-ENTERACCS to be executed as last instruction under NEM.
At NEM Initialization, setting up No-Eviction mode before enabling the MTRRs to avoid the data potentially goes into cache before NEM is ready.

At NEM tear down, clear any Machine Check errors for Machine Check banks 6 till the maximum number of banks (-1, if EDRAM enabled) which may have occurred due to large NEM code and data region sizes causing a write-back for the MLC to LLC eviction.
The Maximum NEM Size in Bytes = Effective Cache size - Reserved size. If ACM takes a number of ways reduce size by - (ACM dedicated ways).
